title: Cubic norm phases become quadratic on subfield hyperplanes
summary: A concrete structured higher-degree family for exact exponential sums, finite-field Boolean functions, and simulation benchmarks.
content: For E/K of degree three in characteristic two, Tr_K/F2(c*Norm_E/K(x)) restricted to any K-affine hyperplane is Boolean quadratic. On that hyperplane x=u+v*s+w*t; every degree-three monomial in s,t is a product of two binary-linear expressions because squaring is binary linear. Recover its quadratic coefficients with O(N^2) evaluations, then apply Gauss elimination. Adding a Boolean quadratic or fourth-root stabilizer phase and further binary affine equations preserves this tractability. Partitioning all inputs into such hyperplanes gives O*(2^(N/3)) evaluation for norm plus quadratic phase.
whenToUse: A concrete structured higher-degree family for exact exponential sums, finite-field Boolean functions, and simulation benchmarks.
limitations: This is a special cubic family, not arbitrary cubic contraction. A partial binary hash need not determine a full subfield-linear value. Padding with free coordinates does not automatically provide a cheaper rank dictionary; see META-01.
